title.zh: 卷四百八十二 列傳第二百四十一 世家五 北漢劉氏劉繼元(父:鈞 兄:繼恩 附:衛融 趙文度 李惲 馬峯 郭無爲)
title.en: Volume 482 Biographies 241: Hereditary Houses 5 - Northern Han and Liu clans Liu Jiyuan (relative: Jun, elder brother: Ji En, relative : Wei Rong, Zhao Wendu, Li Yun, Ma Feng, Guo Wuwei)
title.raw: 卷四百八十二 列傳第二百四十一 世家五 北漢劉氏劉繼元(父:鈞 兄:繼恩 附:衛融 趙文度 李惲 馬峯 郭無爲) Volume 482 Biographies 241: Hereditary Houses 5 - Northern Han and Liu clans Liu Jiyuan (relative: Jun, elder brother: Ji En, relative : Wei Rong, Zhao Wendu, Li Yun, Ma Feng, Guo Wuwei)

sentences.zh: 世家五○北漢劉氏

translations.literal: Hereditary Houses 5: The Liu Clan of Northern Han
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary Houses, 5 — The Liu Clan of Northern Han

sentences.zh: 北漢劉繼元，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Liu Jiyuan of Northern Han was a native of Taiyuan in Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiyuan of the Northern Han state came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖崇，漢祖之弟，漢初為太原尹、北京留守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chong was the younger brother of the founder of Later Han; at the beginning of the Han reign he served as governor of Taiyuan and as commissioner for the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Chong was the Later Han founder's younger brother; in the early Han reign he was made Taiyuan governor and northern-capital commissioner.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，周祖為樞密使，崇謂判官鄭珙曰：“吾與郭樞密素不協，朝廷幼弱，郭得誌，吾無類矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yinyou succeeded to the throne, the Later Zhou founder served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Chong said to his registrar Zheng Xiong: "I have never been on good terms with Commissioner Guo. The court is ruled by a child. If Guo gets his way, there will be none of my kind left."
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yinyou came to the throne, Guo Wei of Later Zhou held the post of Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner. Liu Chong told his registrar Zheng Xiong, "Guo and I have never gotten along. The throne is held by a boy. Once Guo has his way, my whole line is finished."

sentences.zh: ”因泣下。

translations.literal: He wept as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: As he said this, he broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 珙遂勸繕完甲兵，招集亡命，為自全計。

translations.literal: Xiong thereupon urged him to repair weapons and armor, gather fugitives, and make plans to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong then urged him to put arms and armor in order, recruit outlaws and fugitives, and plan how to save himself.

sentences.zh: 及聞隱帝遇害，崇欲率兵南向，會漢太后下令遣馮道詣徐州迎崇子贇為漢嗣，崇信之，謂賓佐曰：“吾兒為帝矣，復何慮哉？

translations.literal: When he heard that Emperor Yinyou had been killed, Chong wished to lead his troops south. It happened that the Han empress dowager ordered Feng Dao to go to Xuzhou to welcome Chong's son Yun as heir to Han. Chong believed this and said to his staff: "My son will be emperor—what more is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: On hearing that Emperor Yinyou had been murdered, Chong prepared to march south with his army. Just then the Han empress dowager sent Feng Dao to Xuzhou to bring back Chong's son Yun as heir to the throne. Chong took this at face value and told his advisers, "My son is going to be emperor—what is left to fear?"

sentences.zh: ”少尹李驤曰：“知幾其神，時不可失。

translations.literal: The junior prefect Li Xiang said: "To know the turning point is divine; the moment must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Junior prefect Li Xiang said, "To read the moment is almost uncanny—and this moment will not wait."

sentences.zh: 揣郭公之心，必不以天下與人，不如領精騎疾度太行，控孟津，以觀其變，徐州位定，然後歸晉陽，即郭公不敢動矣。

translations.literal: Judging Lord Guo's heart, he will surely not yield the realm to another. Better to lead picked cavalry swiftly across the Taihang range, hold Mengjin, and watch how events unfold. Once the succession at Xuzhou is settled, then return to Jinyang—even Lord Guo would not dare move against you.
translations.idiomatic: Read Guo Wei's mind and you will see he will never hand the empire to anyone else. Take your best horsemen, cross the Taihang fast, seize Mengjin, and watch how things unfold. Once the succession at Xuzhou is settled, return to Jinyang—then even Guo Wei will not dare touch you.

sentences.zh: ”崇大怒，罵曰：“腐儒敢離間我父子！

translations.literal: Chong flew into a rage and cursed: "You rotten scholar—how dare you drive a wedge between father and son!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong erupted in fury. "You spineless pedant," he shouted, "how dare you set father against son!"

sentences.zh: ”遽令左右曳出斬之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered his attendants to drag him out and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: He had his men drag Xiang out at once and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 驤曰：“仆負王佐才，今日為愚人畫計，死固甘心，但家有病妻，願同戮於市。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "I possess the talent to aid a true king. Today I offered counsel to a fool and death is acceptable—but I have an ailing wife at home; I ask that she be executed with me in the marketplace."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "I have the makings of a king's right hand. Today I gave advice to a fool, and I accept death—but my wife is ill at home. Let her be killed with me in the market square."

sentences.zh: ”崇並殺之，表其事於太后，明無他誌。

translations.literal: Chong killed them both and reported the matter to the empress dowager, making clear that he had no other design.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had them both killed, then reported the affair to the empress dowager to show he harbored no other ambition.

sentences.zh: 俄周祖為眾所推，降封贇湘陰公。

translations.literal: Before long the Later Zhou founder was raised up by the multitude; Yun was demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guo Wei was elevated by popular acclaim; Yun was reduced in rank and made Duke of Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 崇遣使奉書周祖，乞贇歸藩。

translations.literal: Chong sent an envoy with a letter to the Later Zhou founder, begging that Yun be returned to his domain.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent envoys with a letter to Guo Wei, asking that Yun be sent back to his own territory.

sentences.zh: 使還，知贇已死，崇慟哭，為驤立祠。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, he learned that Yun was already dead. Chong wailed in grief and erected a shrine to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came back, he learned Yun was already dead. Chong wept bitterly and built a shrine in Li Xiang's honor.

sentences.zh: 是夏，李筠以上黨叛，令判官囚監軍周光遜等送於鈞，稱臣求援。

translations.literal: That summer Li Yun rebelled with Shangdang, had his registrar imprison the army supervisors Zhou Guangxun and others and send them to Jun, declared himself a subject, and sought aid.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Li Yun rose in rebellion from Shangdang. His registrar imprisoned the army supervisors Zhou Guangxun and others and sent them to Liu Jun; Li Yun declared himself Jun's subject and asked for help.

sentences.zh: 鈞自至太平驛與筠會，遣其宣徽使盧讚將騎數千隨筠入寇，又遣其河陽節度範守圖援之。

translations.literal: Jun himself went to Taiping Post to meet Yun, sent his commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Lu Zan to lead several thousand horsemen with Yun on the invasion, and also sent his military governor of Heyang Fan Shoutu to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun went in person to Taiping Post to meet Li Yun. He sent his Palace Secretariat commissioner Lu Zan with several thousand cavalry to join Yun's raid, and dispatched his Heyang military governor Fan Shoutu as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 及太祖親討，前軍石守信、高懷德破筠眾於澤州，獲守圖，殺鈞兵數千。

translations.literal: When the Taizu emperor campaigned in person, the vanguard Shi Shouxin and Gao Huaide routed Yun's forces at Ze Prefecture, captured Shoutu, and killed several thousand of Jun's troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu marched in person, the vanguard under Shi Shouxin and Gao Huaide smashed Li Yun's army at Zezhou, took Fan Shoutu prisoner, and killed several thousand of Jun's men.

sentences.zh: 鈞之沙穀砦又為折德扆所破，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: Jun's Shagu stockade was also broken by Zhe Deyi, with five hundred heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's Shagu stockade was overrun by Zhe Deyi as well, and five hundred heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 九月，昭義李繼勳率師入鈞平遙，虜獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Li Jixun of Zhaoyi led his army into Jun's Pingyao and took a great multitude captive.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Li Jixun of Zhaoyi marched into Jun's Pingyao and brought back a huge haul of captives and booty.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年冬，繼勳又敗鈞兵，斬首百餘級，獲其遼州刺史傅廷彥弟勳以獻。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Jianlong, Jixun again defeated Jun's troops, took more than a hundred heads, and captured Jun's Liaozhou prefect Fu Tingyan's younger brother Xun to present.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jianlong 2, Jixun routed Jun's army again, took more than a hundred heads, and sent up Jun's Liaozhou prefect Fu Tingyan's younger brother Xun as a captive.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，鈞侵晉、潞二州，守將擊走之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Jun invaded Jin and Lu prefectures; the defending generals drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 3, Jun raided Jin and Luzhou; the garrison commanders beat him back.

sentences.zh: 三月，太祖詔河東降人徙家於邢、洺，計口給粟。

translations.literal: In the third month Taizu ordered families of surrendered people from Hedong to be relocated to Xing and Ming, with grain issued per capita.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Taizu ordered surrendered Hedong families resettled in Xingzhou and Mingzhou, with grain rationed by head count.

sentences.zh: 四月，太原民四百七十人降。

translations.literal: In the fourth month four hundred and seventy people of Taiyuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month four hundred and seventy Taiyuan civilians came over.

sentences.zh: 七月，鈞捉生指揮使路貴等十一人降，並補內殿直。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jun's captive-taking commander Lu Gui and eleven others surrendered and were all appointed to the Inner Palace Direct Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month eleven of Jun's men, including captive-taking commander Lu Gui, defected and were enrolled in the Inner Palace Direct Corps.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，邢州王全贇率師攻樂平，鈞拱衛指揮使王超、散指揮使元威、侯霸榮率所部千八百人降全贇。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year Wang Quanyi of Xing Prefecture led troops to attack Leping. Jun's Palace Guard commander Wang Chao, the scattered-guard commander Yuan Wei, and Hou Barong led their units of eighteen hundred men to surrender to Quanyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 4, Wang Quanyi of Xingzhou attacked Leping. Jun's Palace Guard commander Wang Chao, scattered-guard commander Yuan Wei, and Hou Barong brought eighteen hundred of their men over to Quanyi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鈞侍衛都指揮使蔚進、馬軍都指揮使郝貴超與契丹悉兵來救樂平，三戰皆敗之。

translations.literal: Before long Jun's commander of the palace guards Wei Jin, cavalry commander Hao Guichao, and the Khitans mustered all their forces to relieve Leping; in three battles they were all defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jun's palace guard commander Wei Jin, horse-army commander Hao Guichao, and the Khitans threw their full strength into relieving Leping—and lost three battles in a row.

sentences.zh: 遂下其城，詔建為平晉軍，以降兵為效順軍，賜以錢帛，靜陽十八砦遂相率來降。

translations.literal: The city was then taken. An edict established it as Pingjin Army; the surrendered troops were formed into the Loyal Submission Army and given money and silks. The eighteen stockades of Jingyang thereupon came over one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. An edict made it the Pingjin garrison; surrendered troops were organized as the Loyal Submission Army and rewarded with cash and cloth. Eighteen Jingyang stockades then surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 九月，鈞復引契丹攻平晉軍，太祖遣洺州防禦使郭進、濮州防禦使張彥進、客省使曹彬、趙州刺史陳萬通將步騎萬餘救之，未至而鈞遁去。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jun again led the Khitans to attack Pingjin Army. Taizu sent the Mingzhou defender Guo Jin, Puzhou defender Zhang Yanjin, guest-pavilion commissioner Cao Bin, and Zhao Prefecture prefect Chen Wantong with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve it; before they arrived Jun had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jun brought the Khitans back against Pingjin. Taizu sent Guo Jin of Mingzhou, Zhang Yanjin of Puzhou, guest-pavilion commissioner Cao Bin, and Zhao prefect Chen Wantong with over ten thousand foot and horse to the rescue—but Jun was gone before they arrived.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年二月，李繼勳與兵馬鈐轄康延沼、馬步軍都軍頭尹訓率兵攻遼州，鈞遣郝貴超來援，戰於城下，大敗。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Qiande, Li Jixun with the horse-and-army controller Kang Yanhao and the combined-forces commander Yin Xun led troops to attack Liaozhou. Jun sent Hao Guichao to relieve it; they fought below the walls and were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qiande 2, Li Jixun, horse-and-army controller Kang Yanhao, and combined-forces commander Yin Xun attacked Liaozhou. Jun sent Hao Guichao to relieve the city; the battle below the walls ended in a rout.

sentences.zh: 刺史杜延韜危蹙，與拱衛都指揮使冀進、兵馬都監侯美籍部兵三千降於繼勳，賜延韜等襲衣、銀帶、器幣、鞍勒馬，其降兵以效順、懷恩為名。

translations.literal: Prefect Du Yantao, hard pressed, with Palace Guard commander Ji Jin and army supervisor Hou Mei registered three thousand troops of their command and surrendered to Jixun. Yantao and the others were given court robes, silver belts, ritual vessels, and saddled horses; the surrendered troops were named the Loyal Submission and Cherishing Grace armies.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Du Yantao, cornered, surrendered to Jixun with Palace Guard commander Ji Jin and army supervisor Hou Mei and three thousand of their men. Yantao and his officers received court robes, silver belts, ritual gifts, and saddled horses; the surrendered troops were organized as the Loyal Submission and Cherishing Grace armies.

sentences.zh: 是月，府州擒鈞衛州刺史楊璘以獻。

translations.literal: That month Fuzhou captured and presented Jun's Weizhou prefect Yang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Fuzhou seized Jun's Weizhou prefect Yang Lin and sent him up as a captive.

sentences.zh: 又鈞耀州團練使周審玉等四人降，賜審玉襲衣、金帶、絹千匹、銀五百兩、鞍勒馬，仍賜名承晉，以為左千牛衛大將軍、領汾州團練使。

translations.literal: Also Jun's Yaozhou militia commissioner Zhou Shenyu and four others surrendered. Shenyu was given court robes, a gold belt, a thousand bolts of silk, five hundred taels of silver, and a saddled horse; he was also granted the name Chengjing and appointed general of the Left Palace Interior Service with concurrent militia commissioner of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Four more of Jun's men, including Yaozhou militia commissioner Zhou Shenyu, defected. Shenyu received court robes, a gold belt, a thousand bolts of silk, five hundred taels of silver, and a saddled horse; he was renamed Chengjing and made a Left Palace Interior Service general while holding Fenzhou militia commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四月，太祖遣馬軍都校劉光將兵戍潞，備鈞入侵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Taizu sent the cavalry commander Liu Guang with troops to garrison Lu, guarding against invasion by Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Taizu posted cavalry commander Liu Guang at Luzhou to guard against Jun's raids.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，鈞招收指揮使閻章以石盆砦降鎮州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year Jun's recruitment commander Yan Zhang surrendered the Shipen stockade to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 5, Jun's recruitment commander Yan Zhang turned the Shipen stockade over to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，招收指揮使樊暉殺監軍成昭，以鴻唐砦降鎮州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the recruitment commander Fan Hui killed the army supervisor Cheng Zhao and surrendered the Hongtang stockade to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month recruitment commander Fan Hui killed army supervisor Cheng Zhao and surrendered the Hongtang stockade to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，偏成砦招收指揮使任恩等百五十人降晉州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year the recruitment commander Ren En and a hundred and fifty others of the Piancheng stockade surrendered to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 6, recruitment commander Ren En and a hundred and fifty men from the Piancheng stockade went over to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，鎮州守將攻破鈞馬鞍山砦。

translations.literal: In the third month the defending general of Zhen Prefecture stormed and took Jun's Ma'anshan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhenzhou's garrison commander overran Jun's Ma'anshan stockade.

sentences.zh: 七月，鈞烏玉砦主胡遇等百三十九人降鎮州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the master of Jun's Wuyu stockade Hu Yu and a hundred and thirty-nine others surrendered to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hu Yu, master of Jun's Wuyu stockade, and a hundred and thirty-nine others defected to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，鈞自李筠敗，狼狽而歸，旦夕懼宋師之至。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Li Yun's defeat Jun returned in disarray and feared day and night that Song forces would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Yun's defeat, Jun had fled home in disorder and lived in daily dread of a Song army arriving.

sentences.zh: 以趙文度為相，召抱腹山人郭無為參議中書事，以五台山僧繼顒為鴻臚卿，參議國事。

translations.literal: He made Zhao Wendu chancellor, summoned the recluse Guo Wuwei of Baofu Mountain to deliberate on Secretariat affairs, and appointed the Wutai Mountain monk Jiying as director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhao Wendu chancellor, called in the recluse Guo Wuwei of Baofu Mountain to advise on Secretariat business, and named the Wutai monk Jiying director of diplomatic relations to counsel on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 因事誅段常，契丹主遣使責鈞曰：“爾不稟我命，其罪三：擅改年號，一也；

translations.literal: On a pretext he executed Duan Chang. The Khitan ruler sent an envoy to reproach Jun, saying: "You did not await my command. Your offenses are three: changing the reign title on your own—that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: On a pretext he had Duan Chang executed. The Khitan ruler sent envoys to rebuke Jun: "You ignored my orders. Your crimes are three: changing the reign title on your own—that is the first;

sentences.zh: 助李筠有所覬覦，二也；

translations.literal: aiding Li Yun in his designs—that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: helping Li Yun in his ambitions—that is the second;

sentences.zh: 殺段常，三也。

translations.literal: killing Duan Chang—that is the third."
translations.idiomatic: and killing Duan Chang—that is the third."

sentences.zh: ”鈞皇恐曰：“父為子隱，願赦罪。

translations.literal: Jun said in terror: "A father conceals a son's faults—I beg forgiveness."
translations.idiomatic: Jun answered in terror, "A father covers for his son—I beg you to pardon the offense."

sentences.zh: ”契丹不報。

translations.literal: The Khitans gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans did not answer.

sentences.zh: 自是使契丹者被留不遣。

translations.literal: From then on envoys sent to the Khitans were detained and not released.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every envoy sent to the Khitans was held and not allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 終以勢力窘弱，憂憤成疾，是月卒，年四十三。

translations.literal: In the end, with his power straitened and weak, worry and resentment turned into illness; he died that month at the age of forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: His power worn down and his position desperate, worry and anger turned into illness; he died that month at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 繼恩嗣位。

translations.literal: Ji'en succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'en succeeded him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖嚐因界上諜者謂鈞曰：“君家與周氏為世仇，宜其不屈，今我與爾無所間，何為困此一方人也？

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu once sent word through a border spy to Jun: "Your house and the Zhou are hereditary foes, so it is fitting that you would not submit. But between you and me there is no such feud—why torment the people of this one region?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taizu had once sent a message through a border spy: "Your house and the Zhou were hereditary enemies, so your refusal to submit is understandable. But you and I have no such feud—why make the people of this corner suffer?"

sentences.zh: 若有誌中國，宜下太行以決勝負。

translations.literal: If you have the will to contend for the Central Realm, you ought to come down from the Taihang and settle victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to contend for the empire, come down from the Taihang and fight it out.

sentences.zh: ”鈞遣諜者復命曰：“ 河東土地甲兵不足以當中國，然鈞家世非叛者，區區守此，蓋懼漢氏之不血食也。

translations.literal: Jun sent the spy back with the reply: "The land and arms of Hedong are not enough to match the Central Realm, yet the house of Jun has never been rebels. We hold this little corner only because we fear the Han line will have no offerings of blood."
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent the spy back with this answer: "Hedong's territory and troops cannot stand against the empire, yet the Liu house has never been rebels. We cling to this corner only because we fear the Han line will have no one left to tend its sacrifices."

sentences.zh: ”太祖哀其言，笑謂諜者曰：“為我語鈞，開爾一生路。

translations.literal: Taizu was moved by these words and said with a smile to the spy: "Tell Jun for me: I leave you a path through life."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was touched by the reply and told the spy with a smile, "Tell Jun for me: I am leaving him a way out."

sentences.zh: ”故終其世不加兵焉。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout Jun's lifetime no troops were sent against him.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason Taizu never sent troops against him for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 繼恩本姓薛。

translations.literal: Ji'en was originally surnamed Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'en had originally borne the surname Xue.

sentences.zh: 父釗，娶崇女，晉初為護聖營卒。

translations.literal: His father Zhao married Chong's daughter; at the beginning of Jin he was a soldier in the Imperial Guard camp.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xue Zhao married Chong's daughter and, in the early Jin years, served as a soldier in the Imperial Guard camp.

sentences.zh: 漢祖典禁兵，以釗崇婿，釋其籍，館門下。

translations.literal: When the Han founder took charge of the forbidden troops, because Zhao was Chong's son-in-law he released him from the registers and lodged him at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder took command of the palace guard, he freed Zhao from the rolls as Chong's son-in-law and housed him at his residence.

sentences.zh: 漢祖後領方鎮，爵位通顯，釗罕得見其妻，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Later the Han founder held a frontier command and his rank became eminent; Zhao rarely saw his wife and was habitually discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the Han founder rose to a frontier command and high rank, Zhao seldom saw his wife and brooded in resentment.

sentences.zh: 一日乘醉求見，即引佩刀刺妻，妻奮衣得脫，釗乃自剄。

translations.literal: One day, drunk, he demanded an audience and at once drew his girdle knife to stab his wife; she tore free of her robe and escaped, and Zhao then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: One day he came drunk to demand an audience, drew his belt knife, and lunged at his wife; she tore free of her robe and fled, and Zhao cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 繼恩時尚幼，漢祖令鈞養為子，遂冒姓劉。

translations.literal: Ji'en was still young; the Han founder ordered Jun to raise him as a son, and he thereupon took the surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'en was still a child; the Han founder had Jun adopt him, and he took the Liu surname.

sentences.zh: 八月，太祖詔伐繼恩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Taizu issued an edict to campaign against Ji'en.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Taizu ordered a campaign against Ji'en.

sentences.zh: 以內客省使盧懷忠等二十二人將禁兵赴潞州，昭義節度李繼勳為行營前軍都部署，侍衛步軍都指揮使黨進副之，宣徽南院使曹彬為都監；

translations.literal: The Inner Reception commissioner Lu Huaizhong and twenty-one others led the forbidden troops to Luzhou. Li Jixun of Zhaoyi was made overall commander of the forward army of the campaign headquarters; the commander of the palace infantry Dang Jin was his deputy; the Southern Bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Cao Bin was overall supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: Inner Reception commissioner Lu Huaizhong and twenty-one others led the palace troops to Luzhou. Li Jixun of Zhaoyi was named forward-army commander of the field headquarters; palace infantry commander Dang Jin served as his deputy; Southern Bureau Secretariat commissioner Cao Bin was overall supervisor;

sentences.zh: 棣州防禦使何繼筠為前鋒部署，懷州防禦使康延沼為都監；

translations.literal: the Dizhou defender He Jiyun was vanguard commander and the Huaizhou defender Kang Yanhao was supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: Dizhou defender He Jiyun was vanguard commander and Huaizhou defender Kang Yanhao supervisor;

sentences.zh: 建雄軍節度趙讚為汾州路部署，絳州防禦使司超副之，隰州刺史李謙溥為都監。

translations.literal: the Jianxiong Army military governor Zhao Zan was commander of the Fenzhou route, the Jiangzhou defender Si Chao was his deputy, and the Yinzhou prefect Li Qianpu was supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxiong Army military governor Zhao Zan commanded the Fenzhou route, Jiangzhou defender Si Chao was his deputy, and Yinzhou prefect Li Qianpu was route supervisor.

sentences.zh: 九月，繼勳敗繼恩軍於洞渦河，其左勝軍使李瓊來降，賜襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jixun defeated Ji'en's army at the Dongwo River. Ji'en's Left Victory Army commissioner Li Qiong came over and was given court robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jixun routed Ji'en's army at the Dongwo River. Ji'en's Left Victory Army commissioner Li Qiong defected and received court robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse.

sentences.zh: 初，鈞謂郭無為曰：“繼恩庸懦，何堪付後事？

translations.literal: Earlier Jun had said to Guo Wuwei: "Ji'en is mediocre and timid—how can he be entrusted with what comes after?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jun had told Guo Wuwei, "Ji'en is mediocre and timid—how can the succession be left to him?"

sentences.zh: ”無為亦以為然。

translations.literal: Wuwei too had thought so.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei had agreed.

sentences.zh: 至是繼恩獨處一室行喪，左右親信皆在太原，無得從者。

translations.literal: At this time Ji'en sat alone in a chamber observing mourning; his close attendants were all in Taiyuan and none could accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Ji'en was keeping solitary mourning in one room; his trusted attendants were all in Taiyuan, and none were with him.

sentences.zh: 或勸召之，繼恩猶豫不決。

translations.literal: Some urged that they be summoned, but Ji'en hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to summon them, but Ji'en wavered and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 有侯霸榮者，邢州龍岡人。

translations.literal: There was one Hou Barong, a native of Longgang in Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Hou Barong from Longgang in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 多力善射，走及奔馬，嚐為盜並、汾間，鈞用為散指揮使，戍樂平。

translations.literal: Strong and skilled in archery, he could run with a galloping horse. He had once been a bandit between Bing and Fen; Jun employed him as scattered-guard commander and stationed him at Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful and a fine archer, he could keep pace with a galloping horse. He had once robbed along the Bing-Fen corridor; Jun made him scattered-guard commander and posted him at Leping.

sentences.zh: 建隆中，率所部來歸，補內殿直。

translations.literal: During Jianlong he led his command to surrender and was appointed to the Inner Palace Direct Corps.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianlong reign he brought his unit over and was enrolled in the Inner Palace Direct Corps.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復奔太原，鈞署供奉官。

translations.literal: Before long he fled again to Taiyuan; Jun appointed him a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fled back to Taiyuan, and Jun made him a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 至是謀持繼恩首獻太祖，遂乘繼恩無備，白晝挺刃而入，反扃其門，繼恩繞屏環走，霸榮以刃揕胸弑之，年三十四，時立六十日矣。

translations.literal: At this time he plotted to take Ji'en's head and present it to Taizu. Seizing Ji'en unawares in broad daylight, he strode in with blade drawn, barred the door behind him, and as Ji'en circled the screens in flight Barong stabbed him in the chest and killed him. He was thirty-four; he had reigned only sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: He now plotted to kill Ji'en and present his head to Taizu. Finding Ji'en off guard in broad daylight, he burst in with drawn blade and barred the door behind him. Ji'en fled around the screens; Barong drove the blade into his chest and killed him. Ji'en was thirty-four and had ruled only sixty days.

sentences.zh: 無為遣卒登梯入，殺霸榮，立其弟繼元。

translations.literal: Wuwei sent soldiers up a ladder to enter, killed Barong, and enthroned his younger brother Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei sent men up a ladder, killed Barong, and enthroned Ji'en's younger brother Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 繼元本姓何。

translations.literal: Jiyuan was originally surnamed He.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan had originally borne the surname He.

sentences.zh: 初，薛釗死，崇以女再妻何氏，生繼元。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xue Zhao died, Chong gave his daughter in marriage again to the He clan, and Jiyuan was born.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Zhao's death, Chong gave his daughter in marriage again to a man of the He clan, and Jiyuan was born.

sentences.zh: 何死，鈞亦養繼元為子。

translations.literal: When He died, Jun also raised Jiyuan as a son.
translations.idiomatic: When the He father died, Jun adopted Jiyuan as his son as well.

sentences.zh: 繼元既襲位，改元廣運，復結契丹為援。

translations.literal: Once Jiyuan had succeeded to the throne he changed the era name to Guangyun and renewed ties with the Khitans as allies.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiyuan took the throne he proclaimed the Guangyun era and renewed the Khitan alliance.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年春，太祖詔李繼勳、趙讚、郭進、司超等將兵先赴太原，太祖遂親征。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Kaibao Taizu ordered Li Jixun, Zhao Zan, Guo Jin, Si Chao, and others to lead troops first to Taiyuan; Taizu then campaigned in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Kaibao 2, Taizu ordered Li Jixun, Zhao Zan, Guo Jin, Si Chao, and others to march on Taiyuan ahead of him, then set out on campaign himself.

sentences.zh: 以繼元太穀令梁文陟為太子洗馬，祁令張續為右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Jiyuan appointed his Taigu magistrate Liang Wenzhi as groom of the heir apparent and his Qi magistrate Zhang Xu as right aide to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan named his Taigu magistrate Liang Wenzhi groom of the heir apparent and his Qi magistrate Zhang Xu right aide to the heir.

sentences.zh: 太祖將至，繼勳敗繼元兵於城下，其憲州推官史昭文以州來降，升本州刺史。

translations.literal: As Taizu was about to arrive, Jixun defeated Jiyuan's troops below the walls. Jiyuan's Xianzhou registrar Shi Zhaowen surrendered the prefecture and was promoted to prefect of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu approached, Jixun routed Jiyuan's army below the walls. Jiyuan's Xianzhou registrar Shi Zhaowen surrendered the prefecture and was made its prefect.

sentences.zh: 乃壅汾水灌其城，又遣海州刺史孫方進圍汾州。

translations.literal: They then dammed the Fen River to flood the city and also sent Haizhou prefect Sun Fangjin to besiege Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Song forces dammed the Fen River to flood the city and sent Haizhou prefect Sun Fangjin to besiege Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼元方恃契丹為援，守陴者揚言旦夕契丹至。

translations.literal: Jiyuan was still relying on Khitan aid; the defenders on the battlements proclaimed that the Khitans would arrive any day.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan still counted on Khitan help, and the men on the walls shouted that the Khitans would arrive any day now.

sentences.zh: 四月，何繼筠敗契丹於陽曲北。

translations.literal: In the fourth month He Jiyun defeated the Khitans north of Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month He Jiyun routed the Khitans north of Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 太祖命以所獲首級、鎧甲示於城下，城中由是喪氣，知嵐州趙文度遂來降。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered the captured heads and armor displayed below the walls. The city thereby lost heart, and Jiyuan learned that Lanzhou's Zhao Wendu had come over.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had the captured heads and armor displayed below the walls. Morale in the city collapsed, and Jiyuan learned that his Lanzhou commander Zhao Wendu had defected.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，南城為汾水陷，水注城中，太祖幸長堤觀焉。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month the southern wall collapsed under the Fen flood and water poured into the city. Taizu went to the long embankment to view it.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month the southern wall gave way to the Fen flood and water poured into the city. Taizu went to the long embankment to watch.

sentences.zh: 登望樓者見繼元殺其相郭無為，城中紛擾。

translations.literal: Those who climbed the watchtower saw Jiyuan kill his chancellor Guo Wuwei, and turmoil spread through the city.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the watchtower saw Jiyuan kill his chancellor Guo Wuwei, and the city erupted in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 俄而城兵自西長連城出，將焚攻戰具，反為攻兵擊走之，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Before long the city's troops came out from the western long linked wall intending to burn the siege engines; they were instead driven off by the besiegers, and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon garrison troops sallied from the western long wall to burn the siege engines; the besiegers beat them back and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 夜半，傳呼壁外繼元降，太祖令衛士擐甲，將開壁門，八作使趙遂曰：“受降如受敵，詎可中夜輕出？

translations.literal: At midnight a cry went up outside the ramparts that Jiyuan was surrendering. Taizu ordered the guards to don armor and was about to open the gate when the Works commissioner Zhao Sui said: "Receiving a surrender is like receiving an enemy—how can you go out lightly in the middle of the night?"
translations.idiomatic: At midnight voices outside the ramparts shouted that Jiyuan was surrendering. Taizu ordered his guards to arm and was about to open the gate when Works commissioner Zhao Sui said, "Taking a surrender is like taking an enemy—how can you go out lightly in the dead of night?"

sentences.zh: ”太祖使伺之，果諜者也。

translations.literal: Taizu had it investigated and they proved to be spies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent men to investigate; they were spies after all.

sentences.zh: 太常博士李光讚上言曰：“陛下應天順人，體元禦極，戰無不勝，謀無不臧，四方恃險之邦，僭竊帝王之號者，昔日與中國為鄰，今日與陛下為臣。

translations.literal: The Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Li Guangzan submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty responds to Heaven and accords with the people, embodies the primal and governs the utmost. In battle there is no defeat; in counsel there is no failure. The lands on all sides that rely on perilous terrain and usurp the title of emperor—yesterday they were neighbors of the Central Realm, today they are subjects of Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Li Guangzan submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty answers Heaven and follows the people's will, embodies the primal order and holds the throne. In battle you never lose; in counsel you never fail. Every corner of the realm that once leaned on mountains and rivers to steal an imperial title—yesterday they neighbored the empire, today they are Your Majesty's subjects."

sentences.zh: 蕞爾晉陽，豈須親討，重勞飛免，久駐師徒。

translations.literal: This tiny Jinyang—does it require a personal campaign, heavily taxing the swift hare, and keeping the army long encamped?
translations.idiomatic: This puny Jinyang hardly needs Your Majesty in person—why weary the swift steed and keep the army standing so long?

sentences.zh: 且太原得之未必為多，失之未足為辱。

translations.literal: Moreover, to gain Taiyuan may not add much; to lose it would not be much disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, taking Taiyuan would add little; failing to take it would hardly be a disgrace.

sentences.zh: 今時屬炎蒸，候當暑雨，倘河津泛溢，道路阻艱，輦運稽留，恐勞宸慮。

translations.literal: Now the season is one of blazing heat and the weather is due for summer rains. If the river crossings flood and the roads become difficult, with transport delayed, I fear Your Majesty's mind will be burdened.
translations.idiomatic: The season is scorching and summer rains are due. If the river crossings flood and the roads become impassable, supply trains will stall and Your Majesty's peace of mind will suffer.

sentences.zh: ”太祖覽奏甚喜，命宰相趙普撫諭諸將欲班師。

translations.literal: Taizu read the memorial with great pleasure and ordered the chancellor Zhao Pu to reassure the generals of the plan to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu read the memorial with delight and told chancellor Zhao Pu to reassure the generals that the army would withdraw.

sentences.zh: 禁軍校趙翰等叩頭願乘城急擊，以盡死力，太祖曰：“汝曹我所訓練，無不一當百，以備肘腋、同休戚也。

translations.literal: The forbidden-army officers Zhao Han and others kowtowed, begging to strike the walls at once and spend their lives to the last. Taizu said: "You are men I have trained—each of you is worth a hundred—kept at my side to share fortune and misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard officers Zhao Han and others kowtowed, begging to storm the walls at once and give their last measure of strength. Taizu said, "You are men I trained myself—each of you is worth a hundred—and I keep you at my side to share fortune and ruin."

sentences.zh: 我寧不取太原，豈忍驅汝曹冒鋒鏑而蹈必死之地乎？

translations.literal: I would rather not take Taiyuan than drive you to brave blades and arrows and tread ground where death is certain.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather leave Taiyuan untaken than drive you into blades and arrows and certain death.

sentences.zh: ”士皆感泣，遂班師。

translations.literal: The troops were all moved to tears, and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The men wept at his words, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，繼元胡桃砦指揮使史溫等以其民內附。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Jiyuan's Hetao stockade commander Shi Wen and others brought their people to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2, Jiyuan's Hetao stockade commander Shi Wen and others led their people to defect to the Song.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂齊王廷美曰：“太原，我必取之。

translations.literal: Taizong said to the Prince of Qi, Tingmei: "Taiyuan—I shall certainly take it."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told the Prince of Qi, Tingmei, "Taiyuan—I will take it."

sentences.zh: ”四年，始議討伐，曹彬以為可，太宗意遂決，語在《彬傳》。

translations.literal: In the fourth year deliberations on a punitive campaign began. Cao Bin held that it was feasible, and Taizong's mind was settled—the account is in the Biography of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the court began debating an expedition. Cao Bin said it could be done, and Taizong made up his mind; the fuller account is in Cao Bin's biography.

sentences.zh: 宰相薛居正曰：“昔周世宗舉兵，太原倚契丹之援，堅壁不戰，以至師老而歸。

translations.literal: The chancellor Xue Juzheng said: "Formerly Emperor Shizong of Zhou raised troops; Taiyuan relied on Khitan aid, held fast behind its walls and would not fight, until the army grew weary and withdrew."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xue Juzheng said, "When Emperor Shizong of Zhou campaigned, Taiyuan leaned on Khitan help, shut itself behind its walls, and refused battle until the army wore out and withdrew."

sentences.zh: 及太祖破契丹於雁門關南，盡驅其民分布河、洛之間，雖巢穴尚存，而危困已甚，得之不足以辟土，舍之不足以為患，願陛下熟慮之。

translations.literal: When Taizu defeated the Khitans south of Yanmen Pass he drove out all their people and dispersed them between the Yellow River and Luoyang. Though their lair still stood, they were already in grave distress. To gain it would not expand our territory; to leave it would not create a threat. I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu routed the Khitans south of Yanmen Pass, he drove out the local population and resettled them between the Yellow River valley and Luoyang. Their stronghold remained, but they were already desperate. Taking Taiyuan would not widen the empire; leaving it would not breed a real threat. I urge Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: ”太宗曰：“今者事同而勢異，彼弱而我強。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Today's business is the same, but the circumstances differ—they are weak and we are strong."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied, "The task is the same as before, but the balance of power has shifted—they are weak and we are strong."

sentences.zh: 昔先皇破契丹，徙其人而空其地者，正為今日事也。

translations.literal: In the past, when the late emperor defeated the Khitans and relocated their people to empty their land, it was precisely for today's affair.
translations.idiomatic: When our late emperor broke the Khitans and resettled their people to depopulate the region, he was preparing for exactly this day.

sentences.zh: 朕計決矣，卿勿復言。

translations.literal: My plan is decided; you need not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up—say no more.

sentences.zh: ”遂遣宣徽南院使潘美等率諸將分兵圍汾、沁、嵐諸州，車駕遂親征，以驍將郭進扼石嶺關，斷契丹援路。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Pan Mei, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, and others to lead the generals in dividing forces to besiege the prefectures of Fen, Qin, and Lan; the emperor then campaigned in person, and sent the fierce general Guo Jin to hold Shiling Pass and cut off the Khitan relief route.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pan Mei, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, and others to lead the generals in dividing their forces to besiege Fen, Qin, Lan, and the other prefectures. The emperor then took the field in person and placed Guo Jin at Shiling Pass to block the Khitan relief route.

sentences.zh: 契丹果至，進擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Khitans indeed arrived, and Jin attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans came as expected; Guo Jin struck and routed them.

sentences.zh: 初，繼元遣子續質於契丹，契丹為進所敗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiyuan had sent his son Xu as a hostage to the Khitans; the Khitans were defeated by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiyuan had sent his son Xu to the Khitans as a hostage. The Khitans were then defeated by Guo Jin.

sentences.zh: 繼元又遣健步間道齎蠟丸帛書求救，進又得之，徇於城下。

translations.literal: Jiyuan again sent swift runners by secret paths bearing wax-sealed silk letters to beg rescue; Jin again captured them and displayed them below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan again sent swift couriers by hidden routes with wax-sealed silk appeals for help. Guo Jin captured these too and paraded them beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 繼元外援不至，餉道又絕，潘美等兵數十萬長圍四合，自春徂夏，矢石如雨，晝夜不息，城中大懼。

translations.literal: Jiyuan's outside aid did not arrive, and supply routes were also cut off; Pan Mei and the others with several hundred thousand troops formed a long encirclement on all four sides; from spring to summer, arrows and stones fell like rain, day and night without cease, and great fear arose within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Outside help never came and the supply lines were severed. Pan Mei and the others, with several hundred thousand men, tightened a long siege on every side. From spring into summer arrows and stones rained down without pause, day or night, and terror gripped the city.

sentences.zh: 會太宗奄至，親督衛士急攻，人百其勇，城無完堞。

translations.literal: When Taizong suddenly arrived, he personally directed the guards in urgent assault; each man fought with a hundredfold courage, and no intact parapet remained on the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong arrived unexpectedly and personally drove the palace guards in a furious assault. Each man fought as if he were a hundred, and no stretch of wall was left intact.

sentences.zh: 太宗慮城陷則殺傷者眾，以手詔諭繼元降，詔至城下，守陴者不納，繼元不能知。

translations.literal: Taizong feared that if the city fell there would be many killed and wounded; he sent a personal edict urging Jiyuan to surrender; when the edict reached below the walls, the defenders on the ramparts would not accept it, and Jiyuan could not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong feared massive casualties if the city fell by storm. He sent a personal edict urging Jiyuan to surrender, but when it was brought to the foot of the walls the defenders on the battlements refused to take it in, and Jiyuan never learned of it.

sentences.zh: 太宗躬擐甲胄，夜至長連城督諸將攻之，控弦之士數萬列陣於前，蹲甲交射，矢集城上如蝟毛，每給矢必數百萬，頃之鹹盡。

translations.literal: Taizong personally donned armor and by night came to the long linked siege works to direct the generals in the assault; several tens of thousands of archers deployed in formation before it; crouching in armor they exchanged fire; arrows clustered on the walls like hedgehog quills; each supply of arrows was certainly in the millions—in no time all were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong donned armor himself and came by night to the long linked siege works to direct the generals' assault. Tens of thousands of archers formed up before the walls and, armored and crouched, traded volleys until arrows bristled on the ramparts like hedgehog quills. Each resupply ran to millions of shafts—and in moments they were all gone.

sentences.zh: 捕得城中人雲，繼元以十錢購一矢，凡聚百餘萬，太宗笑曰：“此為我畜也。

translations.literal: Captured townspeople said that Jiyuan was buying one arrow for ten cash and had in all amassed more than a million; Taizong laughed and said: "These were stored up for me."
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners from the city said Jiyuan was paying ten cash per arrow and had stockpiled more than a million. Taizong laughed and said, "So he was hoarding them for me."

sentences.zh: 五月庚辰，繼元宣徽使範超來降，攻城者以超為出戰，禽而戮之。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the fifth month, Jiyuan's Commissioner Fan Chao came to surrender; the besiegers thought Chao was coming out to fight, seized him, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the fifth month, Jiyuan's commissioner Fan Chao came over to surrender. The attackers mistook him for a sortie and seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 繼元遂斬超妻子，投其首城外。

translations.literal: Jiyuan then executed Chao's wife and children and threw their heads outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan then had Chao's wife and children executed and their heads thrown outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 壬午，馬軍都指揮使郭萬超逾城降，繼元帳下親信因之漸亡去，城中危急。

translations.literal: On the renwu day, Guo Wanchao, Commander of the Horse Army, crossed the walls to surrender; Jiyuan's trusted followers in his entourage gradually deserted, and the city grew desperate.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, Guo Wanchao, commander of the Horse Army, climbed over the walls and surrendered. Jiyuan's trusted followers gradually deserted, and the city reached a crisis.

sentences.zh: 太宗又自草詔諭之曰：“越王、吳主獻地歸朝，或授以大藩，或列於上將，臣僚、子弟皆享官封。

translations.literal: Taizong again personally drafted an edict urging him, saying: "The King of Yue and the Lord of Wu surrendered their lands and returned to the court—one was granted a great fief, the other was ranked among the top generals; ministers, retainers, and sons all received office and enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong again drafted an edict himself, saying, "The King of Yue and the Lord of Wu surrendered their lands and came back to court—one was given a great fief, the other was made a top general; their ministers, retainers, and sons all received offices and titles."

sentences.zh: 繼元但速降，必保終始富貴，安危兩途，爾宜自擇。

translations.literal: Jiyuan, if you surrender at once, your wealth and rank from beginning to end are assured; safety and ruin are two paths—you should choose for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan, surrender at once and your wealth and rank are secure for life. Safety and ruin lie before you—choose for yourself.

sentences.zh: ”至是詔入，諸將銳攻不可遏，太宗臨之，恐城陷害民，麾眾少退。

translations.literal: When the edict was delivered, the generals' fierce assault could not be stopped; Taizong came to the scene, fearing the city would fall and harm the people, and waved the troops to withdraw slightly.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached the city, the generals' furious assault could not be checked. Taizong came forward in person, fearing the fall of the city would harm the people, and signaled the troops to pull back a little.

sentences.zh: 是夕，繼元遣其客省使李勳奉表請降，太宗賜勳襲衣、金帶、銀器、錦彩、銀鞍勒馬，復遣通事舍人薛文寶齎詔答之。

translations.literal: That evening Jiyuan sent his Reception Bureau commissioner Li Xun with a memorial requesting surrender; Taizong bestowed on Xun formal robes, a gold belt, silver vessels, brocades, and a horse with silver saddle and bridle, and again sent Interpreter Gentleman Xue Wenbao to bear an edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Jiyuan sent his reception commissioner Li Xun with a memorial asking to surrender. Taizong rewarded Xun with formal robes, a gold belt, silver vessels, brocades, and a horse with silver saddle and bridle, and sent interpreter gentleman Xue Wenbao back with an edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未盡，太宗幸城北，張樂宴從臣於城台，繼元降。

translations.literal: Before the night watch ended, Taizong went to the north of the city, set out music and feasted his attending ministers on the city tower; Jiyuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Before the night watch had run its course, Taizong went to the north side of the city, set out music, and feasted his attending ministers on the city tower; Jiyuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遲明，繼元率官屬縞衣紗帽待罪台下，詔釋之，賜襲衣、玉帶、金銀鞍勒馬三匹、金器五百兩、銀器五千兩、錦彩二千段，文武官各賜衣、金銀帶、器幣、鞍勒馬有差。

translations.literal: At dawn Jiyuan led his officials in white mourning garments and gauze caps to await punishment below the tower; an edict released him and bestowed formal robes, a jade belt, three horses with gold and silver saddles and bridles, five hundred liang of gold vessels, five thousand liang of silver vessels, and two thousand bolts of brocade; civil and military officials each received robes, gold and silver belts, ritual vessels, coins, and saddled horses according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: At first light Jiyuan led his officials in white mourning dress and gauze caps to await judgment below the tower. An edict pardoned him and granted formal robes, a jade belt, three horses with gold and silver saddles and bridles, five hundred liang of gold vessels, five thousand liang of silver vessels, and two thousand bolts of brocade. Civil and military officials each received robes, gold and silver belts, ritual gifts, and saddled horses according to rank.

sentences.zh: 召升台，繼元叩頭言：“臣聞車駕親征，即願束身歸罪，蓋亡命者懼死，逼臣不得降爾。

translations.literal: He was summoned up to the tower; Jiyuan kowtowed and said: "When I heard Your Majesty was campaigning in person, I wished at once to bind myself and submit for punishment; it was only that fugitives fearing death pressed me and would not let me surrender."
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned up to the tower. Jiyuan kowtowed and said, "When I heard Your Majesty had come in person, I wanted at once to surrender and accept punishment. It was only deserters, afraid for their lives, who forced me to hold out."

sentences.zh: ”太宗籍軍中亡投繼元者數百人，選其巨室者以從軍法，餘賜服及錢帛，分隸諸將。

translations.literal: Taizong registered several hundred deserters from the army who had fled to Jiyuan; he selected the ringleaders to be dealt with under military law, gave the rest clothing and cash and silk, and assigned them to the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong registered several hundred soldiers who had deserted to Jiyuan, selected the ringleaders for punishment under military law, gave the rest clothing and cash and silk, and assigned them to the various generals.

sentences.zh: 詔授繼元特進、檢校太師、右衛上將軍，封彭城郡公，館於行在所，給賜甚厚。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jiyuan Special Advancement, Acting Grand Preceptor, and General-in-Chief of the Right Guard, enfeoffed him as Duke of Pengcheng commandery, lodged him at the mobile imperial residence, and bestowed gifts with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Jiyuan Special Advancement, Acting Grand Preceptor, and General-in-Chief of the Right Guard, enfeoffed him as Duke of Pengcheng commandery, lodged him at the imperial camp, and lavished gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 其相李惲等授官有差，命中使康仁寶監之。

translations.literal: His chancellor Li Yun and others were granted office according to rank; he ordered Palace Envoy Kang Renbao to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor Li Yun and others were given offices according to rank, and palace envoy Kang Renbao was ordered to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 繼元獻其宮妓百餘，悉分賜立功將校。

translations.literal: Jiyuan presented more than a hundred palace entertainers; all were distributed as rewards to officers who had distinguished themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan presented more than a hundred palace entertainers, and all were distributed as rewards to officers who had distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 又令仁寶護繼元親屬百餘赴京，所過續食，賜京城甲第一區，歲時優加頒賚。

translations.literal: He also ordered Renbao to escort more than a hundred of Jiyuan's relatives to the capital, with provisions supplied all along the route; he granted a finest residence in the capital and yearly additional bestowals on festive occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Renbao to escort more than a hundred of Jiyuan's relatives to the capital, with provisions supplied along the way, granted them a finest residence in the capital, and added extra gifts on festive occasions each year.

sentences.zh: 六年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Grand Master with Heats and Equipage Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Grand Master with Heats and Equipage Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，建房州為保康軍，以繼元為節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, Fang Prefecture was established as the Baokang Army, with Jiyuan as its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi, Fang Prefecture was made the Baokang Army, with Jiyuan as its military governor.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，繼元疾，遣中使護醫診視，及卒，遺奏以其子三豬為托，太宗惻然哀之，贈中書令，追封彭城郡王，賵賻加等，葬事官給。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua Jiyuan fell ill; palace envoys were sent with physicians to attend him. When he died, his final memorial entrusted his son Sanzhu to the emperor's care. Taizong was deeply moved and mourned him; posthumously he was made chief minister of the Secretariat and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng commandery, with enhanced funeral gifts and burial expenses provided by the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua Jiyuan fell ill, and palace envoys were sent with physicians to attend him. When he died, his final memorial entrusted his son Sanzhu to the emperor's care. Taizong was deeply moved and mourned him, posthumously made him chief minister of the Secretariat and Prince of Pengcheng commandery, granted enhanced funeral gifts, and had the burial expenses paid by the state.

sentences.zh: 時三豬六歲，賜名守節，授西京作坊副使，家居賜祿。

translations.literal: Sanzhu was then six years old; he was granted the name Shoujie, appointed Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops, and given a salary while living at home.
translations.idiomatic: Sanzhu was then six years old. He was granted the name Shoujie, appointed vice commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops, and given a salary while living at home.

sentences.zh: 繼元性殘忍，在太原，凡臣下有忤意，必族其家。

translations.literal: Jiyuan was cruel by nature; while in Taiyuan, whenever a subordinate displeased him, he would exterminate the entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan was cruel by nature. While in Taiyuan, whenever a subordinate displeased him, he exterminated the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 自太祖親征及遣將攻伐，因之殺傷不可勝紀。

translations.literal: From Taizu's personal campaigns and dispatch of generals to attack, the resulting dead and wounded were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu's personal campaigns and the generals he sent to attack, the dead and wounded were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 及窮蹙始降，太宗待遇終保全之，嚐謂近臣曰：“晉司馬昭以劉禪思蜀之對，戲之雲‘何乃似卻正之言’，此不仁之甚也。

translations.literal: Only when driven to extremity did he surrender; Taizong treated him generously and preserved him to the end. He once told his close officials: "Sima Zhao of Jin, hearing Liu Shan's reply about missing Shu, mocked him saying 'How like something Que Zheng would say'—this was the height of inhumanity."
translations.idiomatic: Only when he was driven to the wall did he surrender, yet Taizong treated him generously and preserved him to the end. He once told his close officials, "When Sima Zhao of Jin heard Liu Shan's reply about missing Shu, he mocked him, saying, 'How like something Que Zheng would say'—that was the height of inhumanity."

sentences.zh: 亡國之君皆暗懦所致，苟有遠識，豈至滅亡？

translations.literal: The rulers of fallen states are all brought down by blindness and cowardice; had they possessed far-sighted judgment, how would they have reached extinction?
translations.idiomatic: The rulers of fallen states are undone by blindness and cowardice. Had they possessed far-sighted judgment, how would they have come to ruin?

sentences.zh: 此可湣傷，何反戲侮乎？

translations.literal: Such men deserve pity and sorrow—why turn around and mock them?
translations.idiomatic: Such men deserve pity and sorrow—why turn around and mock them instead?

sentences.zh: 劉繼元朕所虜者，待之若賓客，猶恐不慰其意爾。

translations.literal: Liu Jiyuan is a man I took captive, yet I treat him as an honored guest—and still I fear it may not be enough to ease his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiyuan is a man I took captive, yet I treat him as an honored guest—and still I fear it may not be enough to ease his mind.

sentences.zh: 守節後為崇儀使，改右屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later Shoujie became Commissioner of the Imposing Ceremonial and was transferred to General of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shoujie became commissioner of the Imposing Ceremonial and was transferred to general of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，特遷右武衛將軍，改右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi he was specially promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard and transferred to General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxi he was specially promoted to general of the Right Martial Guard and transferred to general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 衛融字明遠，青州博興人。

translations.literal: Wei Rong, styled Mingyuan, was a native of Boxing in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rong, styled Mingyuan, was a native of Boxing in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初舉進士，調南樂主簿，曆齊澶二州從事、忠武軍掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Jin's Tianfu era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar of Nanle, and served successively as staff officer of Qi and Cao prefectures and secretary of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Later Jin Tianfu era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar of Nanle, and served successively as staff officer in Qi and Cao prefectures and as secretary of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 漢初，為太原觀察支使，劉崇稱帝，授中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was support envoy of the Taiyuan Observation Commission; when Liu Chong declared himself emperor, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Han reign he was support envoy of the Taiyuan Observation Commission. When Liu Chong declared himself emperor, he was made vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 太祖立，李筠據上黨，遣使降劉鈞，鈞自將兵至太平驛與筠會，遣宣徽使盧讚入潞州監筠軍。

translations.literal: When Taizu established the throne, Li Yun held Shangdang and sent envoys to submit to Liu Jun; Jun personally led troops to Taiping Post to meet Yun and dispatched Palace Secretariat Commissioner Lu Zan into Luzhou to supervise Yun's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu established the throne, Li Yun held Shangdang and sent envoys to submit to Liu Jun. Jun personally led troops to Taiping Post to meet Yun and dispatched palace secretariat commissioner Lu Zan into Luzhou to supervise Yun's army.

sentences.zh: 讚與筠不協，鈞遣融和解之。

translations.literal: Zan and Yun did not get along; Jun sent Rong to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: Zan and Yun did not get along; Jun sent Rong to mediate between them.

sentences.zh: 會筠敗，融被擒，太祖責之曰：“汝何故勸劉鈞舉兵助李筠反耶？

translations.literal: When Yun was defeated, Rong was captured. Taizu reproached him, saying: "Why did you urge Liu Jun to raise troops and help Li Yun rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yun was defeated, Rong was taken prisoner. Taizu rebuked him: "Why did you urge Liu Jun to raise troops and help Li Yun rebel?"

sentences.zh: ”融曰：“犬吠非其主，臣四十口受劉氏豐衣美食，不忍負之。

translations.literal: Rong said: "A dog barks at those who are not its master. My household of forty mouths has received rich clothing and fine food from the Liu house—I cannot bear to betray them."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "A dog barks at strangers. My household of forty mouths has been clothed and fed by the Liu house—I cannot betray them."

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不殺臣，臣亦不為陛下用，終當間道走河東爾。

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty does not kill me, I will not serve Your Majesty; in the end I shall take a secret path back to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty spares me, I will not serve you—I will find a secret way back to Hedong in the end.

sentences.zh: ”太祖怒，令左右以鐵撾擊其首，曳出將戮之。

translations.literal: Taizu was enraged and ordered his attendants to strike his head with an iron mace, drag him out, and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu flew into a rage and ordered his attendants to beat Rong's head with an iron mace, drag him out, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 融大呼曰：“大丈夫死或重於泰山，或輕於鴻毛，今之死正得其所爾。

translations.literal: Rong shouted: "For a great man death may be heavier than Mount Tai or lighter than a goose feather—today's death is exactly where it should be."
translations.idiomatic: Rong shouted, "For a great man death may weigh heavier than Mount Tai or lighter than a goose feather—today I die exactly where I ought."

sentences.zh: ”太祖聞之曰：“此忠臣也。

translations.literal: Taizong heard this and said: "This is a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu heard this and said, "This is a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: ”遽命釋之，召坐御前，以良藥傅其創，賜襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered him released, summoned him to sit before the throne, applied good medicine to his wounds, and bestowed formal robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him released at once, had him sit before the throne, applied good medicine to his wounds, and gave him formal robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse.

sentences.zh: 既而欲放融歸，令融先為書諭鈞，言俟周光遜等歸朝，即遣融去。

translations.literal: Later he wished to send Rong back and had Rong first write a letter instructing Jun that once Zhou Guangxun and the others returned to court, Rong would be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Later he wished to send Rong home and had Rong write first to Jun, saying that once Zhou Guangxun and the others returned to court, Rong would be sent back.

sentences.zh: 鈞得書久無報，乃授融太府卿，賜第京城。

translations.literal: Jun received the letter but for a long time gave no reply; Rong was then appointed Director of the Grand Storehouse and granted a residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jun received the letter but for a long time gave no answer; Rong was then made director of the Grand Storehouse and given a residence in the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，郊祀，融獻《郊禋大體賦》，改司農卿，出知陳、舒、黃三州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, at the suburban sacrifice, Rong presented his "Rhapsody on the Great Substance of the Suburban Sacrifice" and was transferred to Director of Agriculture; he went out to govern Chen, Shu, and Huang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qiande, at the suburban sacrifice, Rong presented his Rhapsody on the Great Substance of the Suburban Sacrifice and was made director of agriculture; he then governed Chen, Shu, and Huang prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he died at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子偁、儔，孫齊，並進士及第。

translations.literal: His sons Cheng and Chou and grandson Qi all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Cheng and Chou and his grandson Qi all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 趙文度，薊州漁陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Wendu was a native of Yuyang in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wendu was a native of Yuyang in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 父玉嚐客滄州，依節度判官呂兗。

translations.literal: His father Yu once sojourned in Cang Prefecture and relied on the military governor's registrar Lu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had once been a guest in Cangzhou and relied on the military governor's registrar Lu Yan.

sentences.zh: 劉守光破滄州，收兗親屬盡戮之，兗子琦年十四，玉負之以逃，至太原，變姓名，丐衣食以給琦，琦後唐同光初為藩郡從事。

translations.literal: When Liu Shouguang took Cang Prefecture he seized all of Yan's kin and executed them. Yan's son Qi was fourteen; Yu carried him on his back and fled to Taiyuan, changed their names, and begged food and clothing to support Qi. Qi in the early Tongguang era of Later Tang became a staff officer in a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouguang overran Cangzhou he seized all of Yan's kin and killed them. Yan's son Qi was fourteen; Yu carried him on his back to Taiyuan, changed their names, and begged food and clothing to support him. In the early Later Tang Tongguang era Qi became a staff officer in a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 當是時，燕、趙之士，以玉能存呂氏之孤，翕然稱之。

translations.literal: At that time the gentlemen of Yan and Zhao all praised Yu for having preserved the orphan of the Lu clan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time men of Yan and Zhao all praised Yu for having saved the orphan of the Lu clan.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，琦至職方員外郎知雜。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Mingzong, Qi rose to Vice Director of the Bureau of Works with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingzong, Qi rose to vice director of the Bureau of Works with charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，琦為給事中、端明殿學士，玉已卒矣。

translations.literal: During Qingtai, Qi was Attendant Gentleman and academician of the Duanming Hall; Yu had already died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai reign Qi was attendant gentleman and academician of the Duanming Hall; Yu had already died.

sentences.zh: 文度入洛舉進士，琦薦於主司馬裔孫，擢甲科，曆徐、兗、陳、許四鎮從事。

translations.literal: Wendu went to Luoyang and passed the jinshi examination; Qi recommended him to the chief examiner Ma Yisun, and he was placed in the top class; he served successively as staff officer in the four commands of Xu, Yan, Chen, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu went to Luoyang and passed the jinshi examination. Qi recommended him to chief examiner Ma Yisun, and he was placed in the top class. He then served as staff officer in the Xu, Yan, Chen, and Xu commands in turn.

sentences.zh: 漢初，為河東掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was secretary of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Han reign he was secretary of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 文度捷給善戲謔，劉崇雅愛之，及稱帝，累官至翰林承旨、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Wendu was quick-witted and skilled in banter; Liu Chong was fond of him, and when Chong declared himself emperor Wendu rose through offices to Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu was quick-witted and fond of witty banter; Liu Chong was fond of him, and when Chong declared himself emperor Wendu rose to Hanlin academician-in-chief and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，授中書侍郎、平章事，轉門下侍郎兼樞密使，加司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery with concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and promoted to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhui he was made vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor, then vice director of the Chancellery with concurrent military affairs commissioner, and promoted to minister of education.

sentences.zh: 久之，與郭無為不協，出知汾州，徙嵐州。

translations.literal: After a long time he fell out with Guo Wuwei, went out to govern Fen Prefecture, and was transferred to Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he fell out with Guo Wuwei, was sent out to govern Fenzhou, and was then transferred to Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖開寶二年親征晉陽，遣偏師圍嵐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao Taizu campaigned in person against Jinyang and sent a detached force to besiege Lan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2 Taizu campaigned in person against Jinyang and sent a detached column to besiege Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 文度危蹙請降，待罪行宮，太祖命釋之，賜襲衣、玉帶、金鞍勒馬、器幣甚厚，其官屬賜物有差。

translations.literal: Wendu, hard pressed, asked to surrender and awaited punishment at the mobile palace; Taizu ordered him released and bestowed formal robes, a jade belt, a gold saddle and bridle, and generous ritual vessels; his officials received gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Wendu asked to surrender and awaited judgment at the imperial camp. Taizu ordered him released and gave him formal robes, a jade belt, a gold saddle and bridle, and generous ritual gifts; his officials received rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 文度本名弘，以犯宣祖廟諱，賜今名。

translations.literal: Wendu's original name was Hong; because it violated the taboo name of the temple of the dynastic founder Xuanzu, he was granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu's original name was Hong; because it violated the taboo name of Founder Xuanzu's temple, he was granted his present name.

sentences.zh: 師還，授檢校太傅、安國軍節度，歲餘徙華州，不宣製而告敕同宣製之例。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Acting Grand Preceptor and military governor of the Anguo Army; after more than a year he was transferred to Hua Prefecture, with no public proclamation but an edict of appointment following the precedent for proclamation appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made acting grand preceptor and military governor of the Anguo Army. After more than a year he was transferred to Huazhou; no public proclamation was issued, but his appointment edict followed the precedent used for proclaimed appointments.

sentences.zh: 又徙耀州，凡曆三鎮。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Yao Prefecture; in all he held three commands.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Yaozhou, holding three commands in all.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 文度善為詩，人多諷誦，有《觀光集》。

translations.literal: Wendu was skilled at poetry; many people recited his works; he had a collection entitled Sightseeing.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu was skilled at poetry, and many people recited his verses; he left a collection entitled Sightseeing.

sentences.zh: 文度之降也，其母在太原，世以不能死節罪之。

translations.literal: When Wendu surrendered, his mother was still in Taiyuan; the world blamed him for failing to die for his principles.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendu surrendered, his mother was still in Taiyuan, and later ages blamed him for failing to die rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 子昌圖，至內殿崇班、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Changtu rose to Inner Palace Honored Company and Gatehouse Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changtu rose to inner palace honored company and gatehouse attendant.

sentences.zh: 李惲字孟深，開封陽武人。

translations.literal: Li Yun, styled Mengshen, was a native of Yangwu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun, styled Mengshen, was a native of Yangwu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中舉進士，客遊嵐州。

translations.literal: During the Qianyou era of Han he passed the jinshi examination and traveled as a guest in Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Han Qianyou era he passed the jinshi examination and traveled as a guest in Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會劉崇自立，署州從事，擢知制誥、翰林學士，累至司空、平章事。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong declared himself independent, Yun was appointed prefectural staff officer, promoted to drafter of edicts and Hanlin academician, and rose through offices to Minister of Works and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong declared himself independent, Yun was made prefectural staff officer, then promoted to edict drafter and Hanlin academician, and eventually rose to minister of works and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 時母在鄉里，惲不知存亡，居常戚戚，但以弈棋沈飲為務，政事多廢。

translations.literal: His mother was then in the countryside; Yun did not know whether she lived or died and was habitually sorrowful, devoting himself only to chess and heavy drinking while state affairs were largely neglected.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was still in the countryside, and Yun did not know whether she was alive or dead. He brooded constantly, devoting himself only to chess and heavy drinking while state affairs were largely neglected.

sentences.zh: 劉繼元頻以為言，惲不介意。

translations.literal: Liu Jiyuan frequently spoke of this, but Yun paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiyuan often complained of this, but Yun paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 後方與僧弈棋，繼元命近侍直抵惲前，取局焚之。

translations.literal: Once, as he was playing chess with a monk, Jiyuan ordered a close attendant to go straight to Yun, take the board, and burn it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while he was playing chess with a monk, Jiyuan ordered a close attendant to go straight to Yun, seize the board, and burn it.

sentences.zh: 惲怡然，徐詣繼元謝，繼元因切責之，明日別造新局，弈棋如故。

translations.literal: Yun was at ease, went slowly to Jiyuan to apologize, and Jiyuan thereupon sternly rebuked him; the next day he had a new board made and played chess as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yun remained unruffled, went slowly to Jiyuan to apologize, and Jiyuan sternly rebuked him. The next day Yun had a new board made and played chess as before.

sentences.zh: 太宗克太原，為殿中監，始知母亡，表求追服母喪，不許。

translations.literal: When Taizong took Taiyuan, Yun was made Director of the Palace Directorate; only then did he learn his mother had died. He submitted a memorial asking to observe mourning for her belatedly, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took Taiyuan, Yun was made director of the palace directorate and only then learned his mother had died. He submitted a memorial asking to observe mourning for her belatedly, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 出知廣州，遷司農卿，連知許、孟二州。

translations.literal: He went out to govern Guang Prefecture, was transferred to Director of Agriculture, and in succession governed Xu and Meng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Guangzhou, was made director of agriculture, and then governed Xu and Meng prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 以足疾求解，授忠武軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Because of illness in his feet he asked to be relieved and was appointed campaigning marshal of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a foot ailment he asked to be relieved of office and was appointed campaigning marshal of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong he died at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duangong he died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 惲性疏達，善談名理。

translations.literal: Yun was open and expansive by nature and skilled in discussing abstract principles.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was open and expansive by nature and skilled in discussing philosophical principles.

sentences.zh: 年少時好滑稽，及為相，頗事持重。

translations.literal: In his youth he loved witty humor; once he became chancellor he became quite deliberate and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he loved witty humor; once he became chancellor he became quite deliberate and weighty in manner.

sentences.zh: 初與王溥、李昉同年登第，太原平，相見敘舊，情好益固，論者美之。

translations.literal: He had first passed the examination in the same year as Wang Pu and Li Fang; when Taiyuan was pacified they met and renewed old ties, their affection growing firmer; commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He had first passed the examination in the same year as Wang Pu and Li Fang. When Taiyuan fell they met again and renewed old ties, and their friendship grew firmer—commentators praised this.

sentences.zh: 子存誠，駕部員外郎；

translations.literal: His son Cuncheng was Vice Director of the Bureau of Imperial Transport;
translations.idiomatic: His son Cuncheng was vice director of the Bureau of Imperial Transport;

sentences.zh: 存信，左侍禁、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Cunxin was Left Palace Attendant and Gatehouse Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin was left palace attendant and gatehouse attendant.

sentences.zh: 馬峰，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Ma Feng was a native of Taiyuan in Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Feng was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕劉繼元至樞密使、左仆射致仕。

translations.literal: He served Liu Jiyuan until he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and then retired as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liu Jiyuan until he rose to military affairs commissioner and retired as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太原平，太宗以為將作監，遷太府卿，分司西京。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan was pacified, Taizong appointed him Director of Palace Construction; he was transferred to Director of the Grand Storehouse and given a post in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiyuan fell, Taizong made him director of palace construction, then director of the grand storehouse, with a post in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 峰善服餌養生，體強無疾，性鄙吝，頗好持論。

translations.literal: Feng was skilled in taking medicines to preserve health; his body was strong and free of illness; by nature he was mean and stingy and rather fond of arguing.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was skilled in diet and medicine for longevity; he remained strong and healthy, but he was mean and stingy by nature and rather fond of argument.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi he died at more than eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi he died at over eighty.

sentences.zh: 郭無為，青州千乘人。

translations.literal: Guo Wuwei was a native of Qiansheng in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wuwei was a native of Qiansheng in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少博學有辭辯，為道士，隱武當山。

translations.literal: In youth he was broadly learned and eloquent in debate; he became a Daoist priest and lived in seclusion on Mount Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was widely learned and eloquent; he became a Daoist priest and lived in seclusion on Mount Wudang.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，周祖征河中，無為杖策謁於軍門，周祖一見大奇之，將留館門下。

translations.literal: During the Qianyou era of Han, when the Later Zhou founder campaigned in the Hezhong region, Wuwei came with staff in hand to present himself at the army gate; at first sight the Zhou founder was greatly struck by him and was about to keep him as a guest at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Han Qianyou era, when Guo Wei campaigned in the Hezhong region, Wuwei came staff in hand to the army gate. Guo Wei was greatly impressed at first sight and was about to keep him at his residence.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：“無為縱橫家流，今公握重兵，不宜親之。

translations.literal: Those around him said: "Wuwei is of the coalition strategist school; now you hold heavy troops—it is not fitting to draw close to him."
translations.idiomatic: His advisers said, "Wuwei is a coalition strategist. You now command a great army—it is not wise to draw close to him."

sentences.zh: ”無為遂拂衣去，隱太原抱腹山。
