translations.literal: Wuwei thereupon shook out his robe and left, living in seclusion on Baofu Mountain near Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei shook out his robe and left, living in seclusion on Baofu Mountain near Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 會劉鈞將兵援李筠，將發太原，其大臣趙華諫曰：“筠舉動輕易，今起兵應之，未見其可。

translations.literal: When Liu Jun was about to lead troops to aid Li Yun and was preparing to set out from Taiyuan, his minister Zhao Hua remonstrated: "Yun's actions are rash; to raise an army now in response to him—I do not see how this can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jun was preparing to lead troops from Taiyuan to aid Li Yun, his minister Zhao Hua remonstrated, "Yun acts rashly. To raise an army for him now—I see no way this can succeed."

sentences.zh: ”鈞怒不顧，遂行。

translations.literal: Jun was enraged and paid no heed, and set out.
translations.idiomatic: Jun flew into a rage, ignored the advice, and marched out.

sentences.zh: 及筠敗，鈞狼狽而歸，由是重文學之士。

translations.literal: When Yun was defeated, Jun returned in disarray; from this time he valued men of literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun was defeated, Jun fled home in disorder and from then on valued men of literary learning.

sentences.zh: 且日夕懼宋師至，頗求有智謀者與之計事。

translations.literal: Moreover he feared day and night that Song troops would arrive and sought rather earnestly for men of wisdom and strategy to plan affairs with him.
translations.idiomatic: He also lived in daily dread of Song armies arriving and eagerly sought men of wisdom and strategy to plan with him.

sentences.zh: 段常薦無為於鈞，鈞以諫議大夫召之。

translations.literal: Duan Chang recommended Wuwei to Jun, and Jun summoned him as Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang recommended Wuwei to Jun, and Jun summoned him as remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 及至，與語大悅，尋遷吏部侍郎、參議中書事。

translations.literal: When he arrived and Jun spoke with him, he was greatly pleased; before long Wuwei was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and made a deliberator on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Jun was delighted in conversation with him and soon made him vice director of the Ministry of Personnel and a deliberator on Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 與趙文度同秉政，意好不協，鈞乃出文度知汾州。

translations.literal: He shared government with Zhao Wendu, but their inclinations did not harmonize; Jun thereupon sent Wendu out to govern Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He shared power with Zhao Wendu, but they did not get along; Jun sent Wendu out to govern Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄誅段常，遂以無為為左仆射、平章事兼樞密使，機務一以委之。

translations.literal: Before long Duan Chang was executed, and Wuwei was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Councillor, and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; all critical affairs were entrusted to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Duan Chang was executed, and Wuwei was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, grand councillor, and concurrent military affairs commissioner; all critical business was entrusted to him alone.

sentences.zh: 鈞嚐病，與無為語及後事，謂其子繼恩不才，無為亦言其然。

translations.literal: Jun once fell ill and spoke with Wuwei about what would come after, saying his son Ji'en lacked talent; Wuwei said the same.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Jun was ill he spoke with Wuwei about the succession, saying his son Ji'en lacked talent; Wuwei agreed.

sentences.zh: 繼恩既立，知其事，欲誅無為，畏懦不能決。

translations.literal: Once Ji'en had succeeded to the throne he learned of this and wished to execute Wuwei, but through fear and timidity could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji'en took the throne he learned of this and wanted to kill Wuwei, but fear and timidity kept him from deciding.

sentences.zh: 月餘，侯霸榮弑繼恩，無為使人殺霸榮，並人疑無為初授意於霸榮，後殺之以滅口也。

translations.literal: After more than a month Hou Barong assassinated Ji'en; Wuwei sent men to kill Barong, and the people of Bing all suspected that Wuwei had first prompted Barong and later killed him to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Hou Barong assassinated Ji'en. Wuwei sent men to kill Barong, and people in Bingzhou suspected Wuwei had first set Barong on and then killed him to silence him.

sentences.zh: 繼元立，太祖遣李繼勳等討之，仍詔許繼元以青州節度、無為邢州節度，無為得詔色動。

translations.literal: When Jiyuan succeeded to the throne, Taizu sent Li Jixun and others to campaign against him and also issued an edict promising Jiyuan the military governorship of Qing Prefecture and Wuwei that of Xing Prefecture; when Wuwei received the edict his expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiyuan took the throne, Taizu sent Li Jixun and others against him and also issued an edict promising Jiyuan the Qingzhou command and Wuwei the Xingzhou command. When Wuwei received the edict his face changed.

sentences.zh: 一日，繼元宴群臣，契丹使亦在焉，無為慟哭於庭曰：“今日以空城抗大軍，計將安出？

translations.literal: One day Jiyuan feasted his ministers, and the Khitan envoy was also present; Wuwei wailed in the courtyard, saying: "Today we oppose a great army with an empty city—what plan can we devise?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Jiyuan feasted his ministers with the Khitan envoy present. Wuwei wailed in the courtyard, "Today we hold an empty city against a great army—what plan is left?"

sentences.zh: ”引佩刀欲自刺，繼元遽降階持其手，引無為升坐，蓋無為欲以動眾心也。

translations.literal: He drew his girdle knife intending to stab himself; Jiyuan hastily came down the steps, seized his hand, and led Wuwei back up to take a seat—presumably Wuwei wished thereby to stir the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his belt knife to stab himself. Jiyuan rushed down the steps, seized his hand, and led him back to his seat—presumably to stir the hearts of those present.

sentences.zh: 及太祖親征，長圍既合，無為請自將兵夜出擊圍，欲自拔來歸，值天陰晦而止。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned in person and the long encirclement was complete, Wuwei asked to lead troops himself in a night sortie against the siege lines, intending to break free and come over; because the sky was dark and overcast he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned in person and the long siege closed in, Wuwei asked to lead a night sortie against the encirclement, intending to break out and defect. Dark weather made him abandon the plan.

sentences.zh: 閹人衛德貴告其事。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wei Degui reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wei Degui reported the affair.

sentences.zh: 會太祖壅汾水浸城，城中人情大懼，繼元乃殺無為以徇。

translations.literal: When Taizu dammed the Fen River and flooded the city, fear spread greatly among the people within the walls; Jiyuan then executed Wuwei and displayed his body as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu dammed the Fen River and flooded the city, terror spread through the garrison. Jiyuan then executed Wuwei and displayed his body as a warning.
